newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN SEEN TENDERING FOR 128,000T CORN - TRADE.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN SEEN TENDERING FOR 128,000T CORN - TRADE.

text.p: Taiwan is likely to tender for up to 128,000 tonnes of corn this week along with a small cargo of 10,000 tonnes of soybeans after futures prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) rose last week, traders said on Monday.

The dealers said Taiwanese buyers felt CBOT corn prices would rise further and probably place the tender later in the week after the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) releases on Tuesday its 1997 corn production report.
"Buyers are quiet bullish on the corn (price)," a U.S. trader based in Taipei said. "They are likely to place (the) tender after the USDA report."
Most analysts estimated 1997 U.S. corn production would reach around 9.554 billion bushels, below USDA's July forecast of 9.7 billion bushels.
Taiwan Sugar Corp would tender on Wednesday for 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of soybean for late September and early October delivery, traders said.
Taiwanese soybean buyers would show little buying interest this week since most of them have already bought their September and October supplies, traders said.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about US$11.50 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $22.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized September shipments.
